rows.statutoryAuthority: C.R.S. § 24-72-710; Colorado Judicial Department forms JDF 680 and JDF 681
rows.implementationStrategyNote: The assignment names official_pdf_fill and JDF 681 gets exactly that. JDF 680 is recorded in the committed corpus index as flat_pdf with acroFieldCount 0 and it is: two pages of printed text and ruled lines with nothing fillable on them. It is built as a measured overlay through finalizeFlatOverlay, the same path the Washington vacatur families use, with every write box derived from a rule read out of the page's own content stream. The per-document strategy is recorded in the source receipt rather than left to be inferred.
notableDecisions: JDF 680's 35 blanks are the printed rules the values sit on, measured from the page's own content stream on every build; the build refuses if any rule has moved by more than a point, and the rule travels with each write in the byte proof so a reviewer can check placement against the paper.

The byte proof reads the flat document back from the finalized page text at those coordinates rather than from flattened widget appearances, because an overlay has no widgets and the widget reader reported nine correct writes as invisible. The form's own printed text at the same coordinates is subtracted from the source, so the certificate-of-service sentence printed across its own rule is not reported as ink on a refused field.

JDF 680's fourteen tick boxes are drawn as glyphs, not stroked paths: checkboxCandidates finds none. No geometry was invented for them. They are listed as printedSelectionControlsNotMeasured, named in the instructions as boxes the participant marks by hand, and the build asserts on every run that they are still unmeasurable.
The Governor's pardon is the whole of this route and the platform does not hold it. Section 3's attachment requirement is the first thing the instructions state.

findingsRaisedForOthers: BLOCKING for the fleet, owner of the Captain branch: scripts/lib/pdf-page-raster.mjs does not exist at the current Captain head (5f144ec). The module is at scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs, and FIFTEEN builders on that branch still import the old path, so none of them can run there: ak-courtview, ak-tf805, co_motion_seal_nonconviction, co_multiple_conviction_seal, co_pardoned_conviction_seal, ky_void_seal_controlled_substance, md_second_chance_shielding, me-seal-prost, mi_setaside_marihuana, or_conviction_setaside, pa_age70_deceased, pa_pardon_expungement, va_seal_petition_misdemeanor, vt_exp_decriminalized, vt_seal_nonconviction. Two builders (ak-tf800, vt_seal_misdemeanor) already import the new path, so the migration is half done. A one-line re-export shim at the old path fixes all fifteen at once. This lane changed only its OWN builders, which now try the new path and fall back to the old, catching ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND and nothing else; the other builders are not this lane's to edit.

BLOCKING for the raster gate, owner of the packet-factory builder contract: assembled packet PDFs are NOT byte-reproducible. PDFDocument.create() stamps /CreationDate and /ModDate from the wall clock, and save({updateMetadata:false}) stops those being refreshed but not being set. Two builds of identical inputs were measured differing in exactly six bytes, all of them timestamp digits. A RASTER_PASS bound to one build's SHA-256 is therefore invalidated by a rebuild that changed nothing, which is the opposite of what a hash-bound gate is for. The fix is two lines before save: setCreationDate(new Date(0)) and setModificationDate(new Date(0)). This lane applied it to the three families no VF lane has been assigned, and proved reproducibility by rebuilding and comparing. It did NOT apply it to its earlier families: VF-SRC-A and VF-SRC-B are reading those now, and moving bytes under a verifier mid-read is worse than leaving a known non-determinism in place for the Captain to sequence.
